name: Adaptive-Resolution Data Representation and Description
definition: A data representation scheme where a volume dataset is divided into spatial blocks, each assigned one of three discrete resolutions: High, Medium, or Low. This allows regions of interest to be rendered at higher fidelity while less important regions use lower resolution.
summary: Adaptive-Resolution Data Representation is a block-based scheme that partitions volume data into hierarchical blocks of varying resolutions to efficiently store heterogeneous data while maintaining constant data size per level.
